Initially, comprehensive physiological, demographic, and activity-related data are collected and preprocessed using Min–Max normalization for uniform feature scaling. Linear Discriminant Analysis (LDA) is applied for feature extraction and dimensionality reduction. The Enriched Convolutional Network (EnCon) captures complex behavioral patterns, while the Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU) models temporal dependencies in sequential health data. Dynamic Coyote Optimization (DCO) is incorporated for optimal hyperparameter tuning. The framework is implemented using Python and TensorFlow for efficient training and adaptive prediction.Results: The proposed DCO–EnCon–GRU framework achieved improved predictive performance compared with existing methods, obtaining accuracy (0,95), specificity (0,96), precision (0,97), and F1-score (0,94). The results demonstrate enhanced prediction reliability and effectiveness in personalized sports health management.Conclusion: The research demonstrates that big data-driven deep learning approaches can effectively support personalized, adaptive, and efficient sports health management. The proposed framework improves predictive capability and exercise recommendation while addressing challenges associated with data integration, scalability, and adaptive health monitoring.

title: Beyond Base Camp: A Framework for Thinking Deliberately About Generative AI Adoption
abstract: Originally published on 11 May 2026 at https://sciencera.org/beyond-base-camp-a-framework-for-thinking-deliberately-about-generative-ai-adoption/ . This record is the archival deposit of that article; the canonical version remains at the URL above. This article introduces a framework for approaching generative AI adoption from a perspective that balances optimizing existing work and creating new forms of value. Cost, time, and quality have long governed project work, under the rule that only two can be optimized at once. Generative AI produces gains across all three, and those gains, the AI surplus, sit on top of a human-quality baseline. Where an organization allocates the surplus is a strategic choice. Race to the Bottom sends it to cost and speed and leaves quality unfunded, inviting a price spiral in which volume crowds out value. The two productive patterns keep quality funded: Quality-Led Acceleration buys faster and better output for the same investment; Capability-Led Efficiency lowers cost on the same timeline, preserving quality through expert workflows. Quality functions as the integrity dimension: where it receives investment, value is created or preserved; where it does not, value erodes. The Implementation Spectrum adds depth to that breadth, running from tactical to strategic execution. It is also what separates two meanings of cheaper: AI augmenting expert workflows, and AI replacing people. Together, as Geometry × Spectrum, the two reveal an organization's true strategic position. Levels 1 to 3, Focused Optimization, Dual Integration, and Full Optimization, complete the triangle: the pre-AI Holy Grail, which the framework calls Base Camp. Level 4+ rises from that foundation: from doing things better to doing better things. All of it depends on the human in the loop: judgment is what AI can surface but cannot supply. The evolution of expertise continues the shift search engines began, from knowing the answer toward discerning which synthesis is valuable, asking the right questions, and recognizing when a confident-sounding answer is wrong.

title: A Stability Envelope Is All You Need: A structural correction to the transformer inference model
abstract: Abstract Modern transformer inference is widely treated as a deterministic readout of fixed weights–a view that obscures the real dynamics of inference. This assumption is structurally incorrect. This paper demonstrates that inference, like training, operates within a stability envelope that governs whether the model can maintain a coherent internal state across sequential evaluation steps. The paper introduces Stable Latent Propagation (SLP), a mechanism that formalizes how latent representations are carried forward during generation and identifies the conditions under which this propagation remains stable, becomes fragile, or collapses. Through this lens, well‑known failure modes—hallucination, context drift, inconsistency, long‑range collapse, chain‑of‑thought instability, pseudo‑agency, and context fragmentation—are not anomalies but predictable outcomes of operating outside the inference stability envelope. By reframing inference as a stability‑bounded, path‑dependent process rather than a static lookup, this paper provides a structural correction to the field’s conceptual model of transformer behavior and establishes the foundation for a formal theory of inference‑layer stability.

title: Visual recognition algorithm for weakly labeled multi-source data fusion of remote sensing images
abstract: To address the limitations of existing fine-grained visual recognition methods that rely heavily on strong annotations and exhibit poor cross-domain generalization, this study proposes a weakly annotated multi-source data fusion algorithm for remote sensing image recognition. The algorithm achieves three core objectives: efficient utilization of weakly annotated data, precise extraction of fine-grained features, and enhanced cross-domain generalization. First, we develop a self-supervised learning-based weak annotation processing framework with attention mechanisms. Through self-supervised tasks like rotation prediction and image restoration, we extract effective features from weakly annotated data. The attention mechanism is then employed to filter high-confidence samples, significantly improving data utilization efficiency. Second, we design a multimodal cross-attention fusion model that maps local image features and textual semantic features into a shared embedding space. By integrating cross-attention and gating mechanisms, we overcome modal gaps and enhance fine-grained feature recognition. Finally, we introduce cross-domain contrastive loss, combining contrastive learning with domain adaptation techniques to identify domain-invariant features across source and target domains, thereby improving cross-domain generalization performance. Experimental results demonstrate that the algorithm achieves a 94% classification accuracy on traditional datasets, outperforming existing baseline models while maintaining stable performance in real-world scenarios.
